title: Trump's son 'opposed' Iran war, believed US should avoid another Middle East conflict
content: Donald Trump Jr expressed private opposition to the war with Iran, differing from his father's military approach. Despite sharing his views with close associates, he has avoided public disagreements with his father. The conflict has revealed divisions within the MAGA movement on foreign intervention. Domestic challenges, like rising fuel prices, have affected Trump's approval ratings amid the ongoing war.

title: 'Remain vigilant, avoid crowds': India issues advisory amid France protests
content: The Indian Embassy in France has raised an alert for Indian nationals amid ongoing protests in the nation. Citizens are advised to avoid large gatherings and comply with directives from local officials. With violent outbreaks and curfews emerging in reaction to increasing living expenses, the French government braces for more unrest. Indians living in France should closely follow news updates and keep emergency contacts easily available.

title: Monsoon's gone, El Nino isn't: Why India's weather worries are far from over
content: El Niño is increasingly influencing global weather patterns including agriculture and temperatures in India. Current forecasts predict a warmer winter as El Niño intensifies, which could affect agriculture adversely. Recent monsoon rainfall deficits raise concerns regarding water resources and crop yields moving forward. Different regions may experience varying extremes from drought to flooding in the coming months due to this phenomenon.

title: Google’s order for thousands of Waymo taxis has left many in the US government worried
content: Waymo has ordered approximately 5,100 electric vans from Zeekr, a brand of Geely Holding Group in China. These vehicles will support the company’s expansion of its driverless taxi service across various US cities. US lawmakers and safety experts express concerns regarding potential security risks related to imported vehicles from China. A bipartisan proposal aims to restrict vehicles manufactured in China, emphasizing compliance with government rules about connected vehicle technology.

title: Russian roulette: Trump bites the bullet with Putin in bid to survive US midterms
content: For Trump, the political calculation appears straightforward. If Russian supplies arrive quickly and in sufficient quantities, they could help ease fuel prices and give his party a political boost. If deliveries fall short or prices remain high, the administration could end up granting Moscow significant economic relief without delivering much for American consumers.

title: Missouri court overturns ruling giving couple ownership of neighbour's road
content: In a notable case from Missouri, a couple gained legal rights to their isolated property via their neighbor's land. Although the court initially granted them ownership of the access road, it later corrected this decision. Ultimately, they received a permanent easement, illustrating the difference between property rights and ownership. The couple can access their property while the neighbor retains the land under the road.

title: Iyer's India face a test of adaptation in New Zealand
content: India's most recent T20I series in New Zealand was in 2022. The match in Napier ended in a tie under the Duckworth-Lewis method after rain interrupted play. India went on to win the series, claiming victory in the only match that was not affected by rain.

title: Rafale Marine trials underway in Goa for INS Vikrant operations
content: Indian Navy is conducting trials of the Rafale Marine fighter aircraft in Goa for modifications needed for INS Vikrant. These trials will ensure the aircraft can operate with the carrier's ski-jump launch and recovery systems. The Indian Navy has placed an order for 26 Rafale Marine aircraft, set for delivery by the end of 2028. Rafale M aircraft serves various missions, enhancing the Navy's combat capabilities.

title: Man's $30 drawing later linked to Dürer, may be worth over $10m
content: A drawing bought for $30 at an estate sale in Massachusetts is confirmed to be by Albrecht Dürer. Experts attribute the ink sketch to 1503 and estimate its value between $10 million and $50 million. The anonymous buyer initially believed it to be a modern reproduction, showcasing his artistic instincts. Extensive analysis confirmed the drawing's authenticity and its links to Dürer’s other works.

title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan marks 10 years in Hawaii, donates $1.48m to hospital
content: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have pledged a remarkable $1.48 million to the Wilcox Medical Center, showcasing their ongoing commitment to enhancing healthcare on the island of Kauaʻi. This substantial donation will provide essential equipment, including a mobile MRI unit and a state-of-the-art 3D mammography machine. Their philanthropic efforts have already benefited over 100 local organizations, emphasizing their dedication to listening to community needs and promoting health and wellness initiatives.

title: Part of Fred MacMurray's ranch bought for $21m now lists for $22m
content: Part of Hollywood actor Fred MacMurray’s 1,750-acre California ranch, the 52-acre Flax Estate and Vineyard in Healdsburg has hit the market for $22 million. Owned by philanthropists Jeffrey and Laurie Ubben, who bought the property for $21 million in 2016, the estate features 26 acres of organically farmed Pinot Noir vineyards and three residences.

title: At 69, Delhi’s ‘stuntman’ continues Ramleela tradition of setting himself on fire
content: Ram Prasad Tiwari is a 69-year-old performer who has been doing a dangerous stunt for nearly 50 years. He sets himself on fire before jumping into a pool of water from about fifty feet high. Tiwari performs during the Ramleela season and travels to various locations for his acts. For each performance, he earns Rs 8,000 to support his family.

title: Josh Allen’s unexpected reunion: Why did he recognize a whistle after 12 years?
content: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen reunited with his former junior college coach, Randy Whited, after 12 years during an unexpected moment before the Las Vegas Raiders game. A familiar whistle brought them together, reviving memories of Whited's early prediction about Allen's NFL future and the remarkable journey that followed.

title: Joe Burrow’s ‘different side’ resurfaces as Ryan Clark defends Lane Johnson
content: Joe Burrow’s different side revelation on The Pivot Podcast resurfaces online after Ryan Clark defended Lane Johnson before Stephen A. Smith for choosing mental health over football.

title: Germany on alert for Russian sabotage after drone spotted near air base
content: Germany has raised the threat level concerning Russian sabotage targeting its military to the second-highest rank, following the alarming discovery of an explosive drone near the Wunstorf air base. Authorities are investigating the incident amid fears of further sabotage against military sites nationwide. In response, the Bundeswehr is ramping up security with heightened patrols and surveillance measures as the conflict in Ukraine continues to escalate.

title: Watch: 'Inquilab Zindabad', CJP leaders Das & Ranka come out of Tihar Jail
content: After a week in judicial custody, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were granted release from Tihar Jail by a special executive magistrate court in Delhi. Das joyfully declared that truth has prevailed, while Ranka chanted a memorable revolutionary slogan. CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke recognized their leadership through social media, and their return has sparked celebrations among supporters.

title: Vivek Ramaswamy goes low in Ohio's race to the bottom
content: Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign in Ohio has stirred controversy with an ad that leverages his rival Amy Acton's difficult past. This ad includes allegations from Acton's estranged mother, leading to significant backlash from the public and political analysts alike. Critics label Ramaswamy's approach as both desperate and inappropriate, signaling a distressing trend in political tactics.

title: Sacramento jury awards $33.3m to jogger struck by dead tree limb
content: In a landmark decision, a jury in Sacramento awarded Michael Flynn $33.3 million after he sustained a brain injury from a dead branch falling during his jog in McKinley Park. The city was found wholly negligent in their tree maintenance and safety checks. Despite the injury, Flynn persevered through rehabilitation to earn his doctorate in physics, advocating for greater accountability in public infrastructure safety.

title: Jalaj Saxena equals Bishan Bedi as Kerala notch up innings win against Odisha
content: This was Jalaj’s 35th five-wicket haul in the Ranji Trophy, a phenomenal number that puts him level with the great Bishan Singh Bedi for the joint fifth-most five-fors in the tournament’s history. Odisha, meanwhile, became the 20th Ranji team he has taken five wickets against.

title: How much debt is too much for Tamil Nadu?
content: The debt dynamics in Tamil Nadu present a perplexing scenario of borrowing intertwined with fiscal strategies. By 2026-2027, the burden of interest payments is expected to significantly eat into state revenue. The imminent maturity of most public debt within seven years heightens refinancing risks. To bolster fiscal health, a shift towards productive borrowing and enhanced public expenditure management is essential for the state's economic longevity.

title: eMudhra security breach: What it means for smartphone, internet users
content: Researchers found that eight digital certificates issued by eMudhra had weak secret keys that could be easily exploited. Browser companies like Google, Apple, Microsoft, and Mozilla responded by blocking these certificates rapidly. eMudhra explained that a flaw during the creation process led to the publication of the weak keys. Importantly, no evidence suggests these weak keys were used in actual attacks so far.

title: Big relief for Das, Ranka: CJP leaders released after 7 days; Dipke posts SRK clip
content: A special executive magistrate court in Delhi reserved its order regarding the custody of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The police sought an extension of three days for their custody following a protest at Jantar Mantar. During the proceedings, Das and Ranka challenged the custody extension in the Delhi high court. The high court advised them to await the SEM's decision before seeking further legal remedies.

title: Travis Kelce’s $200M Six Flags faces scrutiny after roller coaster part falls
content: A metal bracket reportedly fell from a car on Cedar Point’s Millennium Force roller coaster in Ohio, prompting a temporary shutdown. No injuries were reported, and the ride reopened after maintenance inspections and safety checks. The incident follows the death of Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem at Six Flags Over Georgia. Travis Kelce’s reported role as a Six Flags ambassador and investor has drawn added attention, although no link connects him to either incident.

title: Randi Mahomes launches Chiefs collection with Game Day Couture
content: Randi Mahomes has unveiled her new Kansas City Chiefs clothing collection in collaboration with Game Day Couture. Patrick Mahomes’ mother shared an Instagram video on Monday, modelling T-shirts, crew necks and dressier tops featuring the team’s logo. She encouraged fans to explore the collection and choose their favourite looks. Randi also continues to support the Chiefs in person, recently travelling to Las Vegas with her son Jackson for their game against the Raiders.

title: California ant war killed 15 million workers in 6 months, researchers found
content: A tumultuous and deadly rivalry unfolds among five Argentine ant supercolonies in San Diego, resulting in an alarming number of fatalities. These strongly territorial ants engage in relentless battles, disregarding the 'dear enemy effect' common in territorial animals. Surprisingly, studies reveal that these colonies have reached an impasse, maintaining fixed borders even amid continuous aggression, indicating a lengthy conflict without an end in sight.

title: Where India stands in Asian Para Games medal tally after 27-medal haul on Day 3
content: In an impressive showing at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games, India has claimed 27 medals, comprising five gold, pushing their total count to 62 after three days. Standing in fifth place, Indian athletes showcased their prowess, with athletics leading the charge and bringing home 18 medals along with new Games records. Other disciplines, including archery, swimming, and badminton, also contributed to the nation's medal haul.

title: Israel planned intense strikes against Iran on Oct 10, but Trump said no: Report
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was preparing an aggressive attack on Iranian targets amid growing tensions. However, US President Donald Trump opposed these military actions prior to the midterm elections. Reports indicate that Israeli military forces were ready to launch strikes on October 10, focusing on critical Iranian infrastructure. Diplomatic efforts regarding Iran's nuclear program and US sanctions remain contentious and unresolved.

title: London council moves to scrap demolition of 2 estates after 12-year fight
content: In a pivotal decision, Lambeth Council has announced plans to halt the demolition of the Central Hill and Cressingham Gardens housing estates. The focus will shift toward improving existing homes and fostering community ties, sparing residents from the threat of eviction. This significant turnaround, subject to Cabinet approval on October 21, marks a commitment to preserve community integrity and architectural character.

title: Dallas' Forest Theater set to relight tower after 50 years in $45m revamp
content: On November 1, Dallas's iconic Forest Theater is poised to make its grand return following significant restoration efforts. With a staggering $45 million injection aimed at modernizing its cultural offerings, the reopening promises live performances and food vendors to engage the community. The relighting of the Tower and marquee heralds a rejuvenated era, fostering support for local artists and revitalizing the South Dallas cultural scene.

title: Asian Para Games: Simran, Praveen, Sachin shine as India's medal tally swells to 62
content: India's athletics team celebrated a remarkable achievement by winning five gold medals at the Asian Para Games. Sprinter Simran and high-jumper Praveen Kumar set new Games records in their categories. The morning session also saw four silver medals added to the total. Success flowed from other disciplines too, such as badminton, para-archery, and para-swimming. With more competitions ahead, Indian athletes aim for even greater achievements.

title: Florida couple missed 66 mortgage payments; man's bank lawsuit rejected
content: A Florida couple missed 66 monthly mortgage payments on their Naples property, triggering a foreclosure dispute that began in 2009. During the legal battle, Gregory Brian Myers agreed to deposit $5,000 monthly while appealing the foreclosure. He later sued U.S. Bank, alleging it had violated their agreement. On October 19, 2026, a federal appeals court upheld the dismissal of his lawsuit.

title: London taxi driver's £40 Amritsar painting sold for £75,000 in 2016
content: In a remarkable twist of fate, a British taxi driver's modest £40 purchase at a car boot sale has turned into a windfall, as the artwork, featuring the iconic Golden Temple in Amritsar, fetched an astonishing £75,000 at auction. Thought to be the work of artist Baba Bishan Singh, this event highlights the pivotal role of expert appraisals in unveiling the true worth of hidden treasures in art.

title: GRAP-1 invoked in Delhi-NCR: What is banned, what is allowed from November 1
content: Delhi-NCR has invoked Stage 1 of the Graded Response Action Plan due to poor air quality levels. Restrictions will affect coal-fired tandoors and diesel generator use at eateries to mitigate pollution. Vehicle restrictions will come into effect from November 1, especially targeting non-compliant vehicles. Staggered office timings and increased parking charges aim to reduce congestion and emissions. Authorities plan to closely monitor air quality and implement additional measures as needed.

title: Hindus, Muslims celebrate festivals of both faiths in this Madurai village
content: Hindu residents of Thenur near Madurai offered traditional gifts for the inauguration of a renovated mosque. This event highlighted the communal harmony that exists between the village's Hindu and Muslim communities. Villagers participated in diverse religious practices and shared contributions during various festivals throughout the year. A community feast followed the mosque's inauguration, emphasizing mutual respect and unity.

title: Russia to send first diesel shipment to US on Thursday amid global supply crunch
content: On Thursday, Russia is preparing to deliver its inaugural 40,000-tonne diesel shipment to the United States as part of a deal aimed at alleviating worldwide diesel shortages. However, Ukraine has raised alarms that this could inadvertently support Russian military operations in the ongoing conflict. With more diesel shipments anticipated, the energy markets in Europe may experience notable fluctuations.

title: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper may launch November 1; check timings, fares
content: The Vande Bharat sleeper train has a 16-coach configuration, comprising 11 AC three-tier coaches, four AC two-tier coaches and one AC First Class coach. Designed for operations at speeds of up to 160 kmph, the train has a maximum testing speed of 180 kmph, placing it in the semi-high-speed category. However, much of the Indian Railways network currently lacks the infrastructure needed to support train operations at these speeds
